_about: Post-draft power rankings for the homepage. Built from the recap skill's out/recap-data-<yr>.json (final roster grade, ordered by grade then weighted lineup value — same order as the recap index) plus each prose file's boardLine. Newest season first. Regenerate when recaps are rebuilt.

rows.team: Live By McCaff Die By Muh Calf
rows.boardLine: The best WR room in the league by a wide margin, carrying a middling RB group and a TE room whose value is all in its starter.
The best RB room in the league by a wide margin, three deep with top-ten backs, over a WR group tied for the league's thinnest.
Top-heavy and well-placed: two elite starters and the second-best QB slot, every major bet in a top-ten Vegas offense, and a bench built from reaches.
Second-best RB room and the league's best TE slot, built on three offenses Vegas ranks in the bottom ten.
The best single player in the league at the top of a fifth-ranked RB room; the WR group ranks eighth and leans on Arizona, Vegas's lowest-scoring offense.
Two elite starters in McCaffrey and St. Brown over a flat middle: every position group lands in the middle of the pack.
Third-best RB room and a solid WR trio undercut by the lowest-rated QB room in the league.
A three-deep RB room that ranks fourth, paired with the league's thinnest WR group and a QB slot at waiver level.
Second-best WR room in the league carrying the worst RB and TE groups; three-quarters of the roster's value sits at one position.
The best QB slot and second-best TE slot in the league, but no top-tier RB or WR: the top two starters project lowest of any roster.
